subject: Term & Renewal redlines — staggered opt-out counterproposal
messages:
From: Cassandra Lee <cassie@brightline.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline.com
Date: 2026-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — term & auto-renew

Logan,

Attached are our legal redlines for the MSA and the Order Form. Primary asks:
- Replace the standard 60-day opt-out with a 90-day notice for auto-renew (Brightline needs a longer procurement cycle).
- Remove the unlimited termination-for-convenience without fee; propose a 6-month minimum charge if terminated for convenience in the first year.
- Ask for 120 days of post-termination data export and 30 days of transition assistance.

We highlighted the clauses in the PDF and added inline comments (see attachment). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept longer notice or provide alternative mitigations (e.g., prorated termination fees, shortened transition SLAs)?

Thanks,
Cassandra
Procurement & Contracts
Brightline Systems

[Attachment: brightline_msa_redline_20260601.pdf (pdf)]

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Cassandra Lee <cassie@brightline.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — term & auto-renew

Cassandra — thank you for the redlines and the clear comments. I’ve looped in Karthik (contracts) and Marissa (sales ops) to coordinate a short review and propose a compromise.

High-level thoughts:
- 90-day opt-out is longer than our standard renewal cadence but not immutable — we can consider a tiered approach depending on committed TCV.
- Term-for-convenience fee: we’d prefer a prorated unwind rather than an outright minimum charge; that helps with fairness across pilots vs committed deals.
- Transition assistance and data export windows are negotiable; we typically offer 30–90 days depending on the migration plan and whether dedicated capacity is involved.

Karthik / Marissa — can you review the redlines and propose two counter options: (A) conservative — keep 60d opt-out, offer 60d transition and prorated billing; (B) commercial — accept 90d opt-out if Brightline commits to 6 months minimum in the initial Order Form (or higher TCV). I’ll send a single document back to Cassandra with our preferred language.

Logan
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-03T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — term & auto-renew

Logan — reviewed the PDF. I drafted two short clause alternatives and a suggested rationale for legal (attached). Key points from legal perspective:
1) Auto-renew notice window: negotiating a tiered opt-out is clean — 60 days standard, extend to 90 days only for orders > $250k ARR or multi-year terms. This preserves our operational predictability.
2) Termination-for-convenience: we should avoid flat minimum fees. Recommend: if Customer terminates for convenience within first 12 months, Customer pays the greater of (i) 25% of remaining committed fees or (ii) actual cost of any pre-provisioned dedicated capacity for the remainder of the committed term.
3) Transition assistance/data export: offer 90 days of data export for Dedicated/Private customers; 30 days for Hosted customers, with an option to purchase extended assistance.

I attached a short doc (redwood_proposed_clause_20260603.docx) with exact language we can send as a tracked-change suggestion. If Sales wants to soften, we can make the 25% a sliding scale.

-Karthik
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_proposed_clause_20260603.docx (docx)]

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-04T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — term & auto-renew

Team — quick commercial guidance from my side: Brightline is mid-market and appears price-sensitive, but they have a pilot that could convert to $200k+ ARR. My suggestion to land the deal while protecting us:
- Offer Option B (commercial): Accept 90-day auto-renew opt-out but require a 4-month minimum first-payment commitment (not 6) and a 30% ramp fee if they exit within 12 months.
- Keep transition assistance at 60 days (compromise), but include a paid option for 90–180 days at a daily rate.
- We should also include a limited termination-for-convenience cap for Hosted customers (cap = 3 months of average monthly committed fees) — this gives them predictability and protects our ops.

If you agree, I’ll draft an updated Order Form with those numbers and we can send it back to Brightline as a commercial counter.

-Marissa
Account Director, West
Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Cassandra Lee <cassie@brightline.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-05T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — term & auto-renew

Cassandra — thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. We’re prepared to propose a middle path to unblock procurement and preserve operational predictability. Summary of our counter (attached updated Order Form v2):

1) Auto-renew opt-out window: 60 days standard. For Order Forms with initial committed TCV >= $250,000 or multi-year terms, opt-out window extends to 90 days.
2) Minimum commitment / early-exit: For mid-market pilots, Redwood will accept a 4-month minimum payment obligation for the initial term. If Customer terminates for convenience within 12 months, Customer pays a ramp fee equal to 30% of remaining committed fees or the cost to deallocate any dedicated capacity (whichever is greater). Hosted-only customers have a capped termination liability equal to 3 months of average monthly committed fees.
3) Transition assistance & data export: Redwood will provide up to 60 days of transition assistance (included). For Dedicated/Private deployments, 90 days of export assistance included. Extended assistance (90–180 days) is available as a paid add-on (daily rate shown on the Order Form).

We attached an updated Order Form showing the numbers and tracked changes for the MSA. If Brightline agrees to the 4-month minimum on the initial Order Form, we can accept the extended 90-day opt-out for qualifying orders. Please review and let me know if you’d like a short call to finalize.

Best,
Logan
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: orderform_v2_redline_20260605.pdf (pdf)]
